newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Courtaulds seen posting weak H1.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Courtaulds seen posting weak H1.

text.p: The market is braced for a weak set of interim results from chemicals group Courtaulds Plc on Wednesday, with continuing difficulties in the viscose market undermining improvements elsewhere, analysts said.
Analysts' forecasts are for pretax profit of between 65.0 and 70.0 million stg compared with 67.8 million last time, with the dividend rising to between 4.40 and 4.45 pence from 4.30.
In a note on the company, analysts at NatWest Securities warned that the first-half results could trigger a further round of downgrades.
Courtaulds has recently been hit by profit and stock downgrades from brokerages including Kleinwort Benson, Merrill Lynch and SBC Warburg.
Last week ABN Amro Hoare Govett cut its year through March 1997 pre-tax profit estimates by 20 percent because of the continued squeeze in the key textiles business.
Last year the company was hit by a sharp fall in profitability in viscose, acrylic and acetate fibres because of high raw material costs, destocking and depressed consumer spending across Europe.
In a trading update in July the company said the acrylic market was recovering, but viscose remained uncertain.

An analyst with a U.S. bank who asked not to be identified said the performance of the fibres business would again be crucial in determining sentiment towards the company. The analyst said any comment on the expected timing of a recovery in viscose would be keenly watched.
NatWest said anecdotal evidence suggested that acrylic fibre production in August was at its highest level for many years in western Europe, while in contrast viscose markets "remain pitiful".

Analysts will be keen to monitor the performance of the group's new wonder-fibre, Tencel, a man-made material derived from wood-pulp which admirers say offers considerable advantages over viscose and cotton.
Tencel has already carved out an important niche for itself and some analysts expect sales in the year through March to at least double from last year's 100 million stg.

While the focus will be on fibres, an analyst with a European brokerage, who also asked not to be named, said there could be some disappointment over the performance of the coatings and sealants business, which includes its market-leading marine paints operations and aerospace products.

"People are expecting quite a lot from that, but they may not get what they expect. The Far East in particular has not been that great and they are quite strongly exposed out there," the analyst said.
